title: Cusco School of painting
summary: The Cusco School was a colonial painting tradition centred on Cusco, the former Inca capital. Native and mestizo painters trained in European methods took on its religious subjects and gave them bright colours, flattened forms, gold ornament and Andean symbols. In 1688 the Cusco painters' association split along ethnic lines, and indigenous painters gained an independent workshop.

uncertainty.note: Sources describe the school as taking shape in the second half of the 16th century and thriving into the 1700s, with decline from the late 1700s; the span is approximate.

as_recorded.value: second half of the 16th century: school began to take shape; thrived late 1500s to 1700s; 1688 association split along ethnic lines
1649 painters' guilds established; 1824 style nearly disappeared by independence; flourished for over a century

importance.justification: Major colonial Andean painting tradition blending European and indigenous elements.
